{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Harriet Suzanne Katcher Pollatsek''' (born '''Harriet Katcher''', May 2, 1942) is an American mathematician and Professor Emeritus of Mathematics <ref name="mtholyoke">{{cite web|title=Harriet Pollatsek, Professor Emeritus of Mathematics|url=https://www.mtholyoke.edu/people/harriet-pollatsek|website=Mount Holyoke|date=12 July 2016 |accessdate=14 February 2018}}</ref>  at [[Mount Holyoke College]].<ref name="nwm">Charlene Morrow and Teri Peri (eds), ''Notable Women in Mathematics'', Greenwood Press, 1998, pp. 164-169.</ref>

==Education and career==
Born to a [[Jew]]ish family<ref>{{cite book|page=[https://archive.org/details/notablewomeninma00morr/page/164 164]|title=Notable Women in Mathematics: A Biographical Dictionary|editor1-last=Morrow|editor1-first=Charlene|editor2-last=Perl|editor2-first=Teri|publisher=Greenwood Press|location=Westport, CT|isbn=0-313-29131-4|year=1998|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/notablewomeninma00morr/page/164}}</ref> in [[Detroit|Detroit, Michigan]], Pollatsek entered the honors program at [[University of Michigan]] in 1959, the first person in her family to attend college.<ref name="nwm"/> She earned a BA in mathematics in 1963 and her PhD in 1967 under the direction of Jack E. McLaughlin.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=5480}}</ref>
After graduating she held short-term teaching positions at [[Western Michigan University]] in [[Kalamazoo, MI|Kalamazoo]], the [[University of Toledo]], and the [[University of Massachusetts Amherst]].<ref name="seaway">[http://www.math.binghamton.edu/maa_seaway/Meetings/Siena-97b/sie-speakers.html Speaker bio] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150217224046/http://www.math.binghamton.edu/maa_seaway/Meetings/Siena-97b/sie-speakers.html |date=2015-02-17 }}, Seaway Section of the MAA, Fall 1997, retrieved 2015-02-17.</ref>

Following this, she joined the faculty at Mount Holyoke  College in 1970,<ref name="seaway"/> and earned tenure there in 1974.
In 1990 she was named the Julia and Sarah Ann Adams Professor of Science at Mount Holyoke College.
She was dean of studies from 1977 to 1980.
On sabbatical leaves, she has also been a visiting professor at the University of Oregon.

==Contributions and honors==
Pollatsek's research interests include [[finite group]]s, [[finite geometry|finite geometries]], [[Lie theory]], [[difference set]]s and their application to [[error correcting codes]] and [[coding theory]].

With Emily H. Moore, she is the author of the book ''Difference Sets: Connecting Algebra, Combinatorics, and Geometry'' (Student Mathematical Library 67, American Mathematical Society, 2013).<ref>[https://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/difference-sets-connecting-algebra-combinatorics-and-geometry Review of ''Difference Sets''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170627143535/http://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/difference-sets-connecting-algebra-combinatorics-and-geometry |date=2017-06-27 }}, Mark Hunacek, ''MAA Reviews'', October 2013.</ref>

She has been active in developing new methods of teaching mathematics, particularly in developing a new method of teaching calculus called calculus in context. This method embeds calculus concepts in specific questions from various sciences and then goes to the abstract and generalized concepts.

She has worked on summer mathematical research with undergraduates under the [[National Science Foundation|NSF]] program [[Research Experiences for Undergraduates]].

In 2007 Pollatsek was presented with the Mount Holyoke College Faculty Prize for Teaching.<ref name="fourMHC">{{cite web|title=Four MHC Professor Celebrated|url=https://www.mtholyoke.edu/media/four-mhc-professors-celebrated|website=Mount Holyoke|accessdate=14 February 2018|archive-date=15 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180215003421/https://www.mtholyoke.edu/media/four-mhc-professors-celebrated|url-status=dead}}</ref>
